scope: Medicine, law, engineering and technical STEM research; public catalog only; no private models accessed
method: Reviewed existing 117-occupation catalog; browsed official BLS OOH, O*NET, ABET, AAMC and ABA sources. Proposals are editorial designs; their ability to improve student matches has not been empirically established.

sources.title: BLS OOH: Physicians and Surgeons
sources.keyEvidence: Clinical and nonclinical work and multiple specialties; typical bachelor’s, medical degree and residency. A working physician and a first-paid resident are different financial stages.

sources.title: BLS OOH: Lawyers
sources.keyEvidence: Legal work includes advice, transactions, documents and litigation. Typical law degree and state admission; newly hired associates work with experienced lawyers.

sources.title: AAMC Careers in Medicine
sources.keyEvidence: Self-exploration and exploration of specialty options precede choosing a specialty; contains over 200 specialty profiles. This supports exploration, not a validated scoring key for this product.

sources.title: ABA Practice Areas & Career Resources
sources.keyEvidence: Practice areas include civil rights, business, environment, family, intellectual property, health, immigration and litigation. These are branches within lawyer exploration, not distinct SOC occupations.

sources.title: ABET: What Programs Does ABET Accredit?
sources.keyEvidence: Engineering and engineering technology are related but distinct; engineering emphasizes theoretical analysis and conceptual design. Engineering technology has associate and bachelor routes; licensing pathways vary.

sources.title: BLS OOH: Aerospace Engineers

findings.finding: Doctor, lawyer and engineer are not absent from the catalog: physician is specifically family medicine; law is Lawyers; five engineering occupations are mechanical, civil, electrical, biomedical and industrial. Their absence from a particular view must be diagnosed as exposure, unanswered comparisons, confirmation, ranking, or affordability; catalog presence alone does not establish that models received a fair opportunity.

Family medicine cannot stand in for the full variety of physician work. Add a broad medicine exploration entry that routes to diagnostic/longitudinal care, acute care, procedural work, mental health and imaging/laboratory diagnosis. Keep current family medicine evidence and label accurate; specialty preferences are exploratory, not promised residency placements.

The two existing lawyer prompts focus on legal research and case/precedent argument. Add client advice, transactions/contracts, negotiation and regulatory/public-interest applications. Preserve one Lawyer occupation and shared J.D./license preparation; practice-area preferences should not create duplicate Top counts.

Five engineering disciplines leave meaningful gaps in materials, processes, electronics/computing hardware, environmental systems, agriculture and aerospace. Cross-field exploration can ask whether science, tinkering, computing or conservation interest extends to design, modeling and testing; do not require engineering vocabulary or prior technical training.

Ask work interest before willingness to pursue long training, current mathematics confidence, admissions readiness, finances or work context. These are separate dimensions. College willingness can broaden invitations but cannot substitute for domain interest; unfamiliarity should produce a short activity example rather than a negative answer.
findings.basis: Product-design recommendation, not a psychometric finding

findings.finding: Professional-school completion is not the first paid stage for physicians: paid residency and later independent practice need separate budgets. For new occupations, leave lifestyle-sustaining unknown until a source-backed first-paid-stage wage and route budget exist. Occupational medians and wage percentiles must not be relabeled as graduate starting salaries.

proposedOccupations.title: Aerospace Engineers
proposedOccupations.typicalEntryDegree: Bachelor’s in aerospace engineering or related field
proposedOccupations.entryVsExperienced: A degree-qualified entry role is distinct from senior, lead, manager, independent consultant or licensed sign-off responsibility; additional requirements vary by employer and jurisdiction.
definingInterests: Design and test flying vehicles and spacecraft
novicePrompts: Would you like to learn how to design an aircraft or spacecraft so it can fly or move safely and efficiently?
Would you like to learn to use calculations and prototype tests to improve how an aircraft or spacecraft performs?
proposedOccupations.contrastingQuestion: Which sounds more interesting: designing and testing a flying vehicle, operating it, repairing it, or none of these?
proposedOccupations.contrastAnswerUse: Choose any that appeal, neither, or not sure. Treat choices as information about preference; do not force exclusive interest. A neutral contrast is not a penalty.
risks: Interest in space news or flying is not enough to establish engineering-design interest. Defense clearance requirements apply to some jobs, not the entire occupation.

definingInterests: Diagnose and manage hearing and balance problems
novicePrompts: Would you like to learn to test a person’s hearing or balance and work out what kind of problem they have?
Would you like to learn to fit and adjust hearing technology or other treatment and help someone adapt as their hearing needs change?
proposedOccupations.contrastingQuestion: Would you rather diagnose hearing problems and guide treatment, teach communication skills, design audio equipment, or none?
proposedOccupations.contrastAnswerUse: Choose any that appeal, neither, or not sure. Treat choices as information about preference; do not force exclusive interest. A neutral contrast is not a penalty.
risks: Music/audio enthusiasm is not sufficient clinical interest. Separate diagnosis and patient treatment from hearing-aid sales and sound engineering.

salary.reason: No entry wage established by this research. BLS OOH medians describe the occupation’s employed workforce, not new graduates; low percentiles are not automatically entry wages.

proposedOccupations.questionProvenance: Editorial novice-friendly adaptation of occupational duties; not a validated assessment item or verbatim O*NET item.

implementationPlan: Create coverage manifests linking every new occupation to field invitations, two distinct defining-interest activities, contrasts, training routes, clinical scope and verified source tasks. Do not add a title without reachable questions.

Use a broad-to-specific exploration map across existing fields. Surface a representative degree option for plausible design/science/data/legal/medical interests even when a closely adjacent trade currently ranks higher. Invitation eligibility is not Top eligibility.

Present a short realistic activity example when a student is unfamiliar. Ask interest in learning to do that work; collect uncertainty, dislike and context separately. Do not require all work variants as universal gates.

Require occupation-specific corroboration before Top and independent evidence from more than a single broad helping, math or making-things choice. Retain whole-profile pattern, contradictions and clinical role safeguards; treat these drafts as unvalidated until tested.

Freeze the question bank and offered manifest, then author profile-consistent answers without showing answerers ranks, desired occupations, salary or previous model verdicts. Preserve original rounds and show current outcomes against them.

Audit coverage funnels by occupation: reachable, eligible, offered, answered, supported, confirmed, Top, Other, sustainable, hidden/truncated. Report degree and nondegree separately without quotas. Audit contradictory profiles, broad-Yes profiles, unfamiliar novices and long-route unwillingness.

Before enabling lifestyle claims, verify regional training route, licensure, realistic first-paid stage, program cost, funding and salary source/date. Medicine must show residency separately; research careers must distinguish postdoctoral and established roles.

Keep subtype counts deduplicated at the parent catalog level. For robotics report its O*NET detail and broader wage SOC separately. For clinical laboratory work distinguish technologist and technician; do not infer bachelor-route wages from the combined BLS reference.
limits: No model biography or private file was read; no proposed occupation is asserted to match a particular model.
